Generator for PR2312 width exchange plus coherent four-handoff transformation
==========================================================================

generate_words.py is new portable code prepared with substantial AI
assistance, under the repository Apache-2.0 license. It directly transforms
the pinned PR2312 width-exchange BORROW-WORDs and regenerates cleanup. The existing source
builder is not copied or imported at runtime. The independent native chain,
rather than the generator or its hashes, proves all-column circuit correctness
and exact physical Clifford phases.

PR2312 width exchange is credited to Jeremy Kothe (@jeremykothe2), with
AI assistance: alias 651 is re-lent from lender 530 and alias 653 is dropped,
freeing register 554 for cold restoration and changing two width-8 helpers
to width 7. The exact frame re-solve of both borrowed words and the owner
fill for that source width inventory retain the source's credit to Jeremy
Kothe, with AI assistance. This generator consumes the resulting complete
source words; it does not reapply their kernels or width exchange.

The two helper-donor kernels at pivots 518 and 506 are retained from
PR2302. Their kernel shape is credited to mdumitrean (PR1625); their search,
exact pricing and frame re-solve are credited to Jeremy Kothe
(@jeremykothe2), with AI assistance, as stated by the source. The PR2302
source and this necessary derivative generator were prepared with AI
assistance. This generator composes the four block-616 handoffs after those
kernels, preserving all kernel scalar gates and their re-solved frames.

--- PR2226 native-chain notice (verbatim) ---

# Credit: anticipatory dirty borrowing (PR2226)

The construction realised by this native chain is **PR2226, "anticipatory dirty borrowing"**, by Cinna Davis
(@1337isnot1337), prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance (Apache-2.0): the logical reference change
K_G of a lender register (a monomial Clifford: a permutation of the 512 columns with phase mod 4), the initial
compensation terms c K_G z, the early cold tail, the exact cold restoration and the private zero buffers of the
FULL-frame cleanup.  `vendor/pr2226_operators.py`, `vendor/pr2226_replay.py` and `vendor/PR2226-NOTICE.md` are byte copies
of PR2226's `operators.py`, `replay.py` and `NOTICE.md`.  `bw_gauss.py` is a port of `operators.py` (change, monomial,
apply_mono, coord, frame, check) and adds a decoder from a serialized `clifford_exact` monomial to its exact 512 x 512
Gaussian matrix.

What this chain adds (the P3 native realisation, with the Borrow campaign's explicit chronological BORROW-WORD as input):
warp events and zero buffers in `LOCAL-PROGRAMS`, warp recipes in `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json` (lowered with the unchanged
`lower_child`, rank zero, then compared with the exact numpy column product), logical K_G recipes in
`RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json`, an independent local replay in both orientations that checks every warp product on all 512
columns, and the negative controls listed in `INDEPENDENT-LOCAL-REPLAY.json`, `WRAPPER-CHECKS.json`, `WARP-RECIPE-CHECKS.json`
and `bw_tamper.py`.

Lineage retained: icekylinx (PR425/433/514, scalar and wrapper machinery), DreamingOfClouds (PR458/484/593 hyperplane/cold-HPE
extensions), the clifford_exact compiler (vendor531), and the owners named in the package README.  `vendor/clifford/clifford_exact.py`
is a byte copy.


Reproduction and equality
========================

Run:
  python3 generate_words.py --source-root FETCHED_REPOSITORY --out NEW_DIRECTORY

The generator checks the pinned source manifest and both consumed compressed
source-word hashes. It writes base.json.gz, extra.json.gz and GENERATION.json.
Canonical JSON hashes cover every output field, including frames, scalar
gates, operators, endpoints, cleanup and invoices. These hashes determine
regenerated circuit equality. The compressed container hashes are recorded
for provenance; Python/zlib changes can produce different gzip streams for
the same circuit. The OS header byte is normalized to 255. In the recorded generation
environment both output containers also exactly match the composed
word hashes. Recompression alone does not require repeating native phases.

The four binary G maps are explicit construction constants, checked for
invertibility and the measured source-to-handoff chart identity on each run.
The native replay independently lowers their exact physical representatives.
Two old warp-basis representatives are rewritten only after verifying equal
GF(2) spans, preserving the frozen input serialization. No JSON patch file or
unrecorded local dependency is needed.

Composition binding
===================

The source-manifest and source-word constants bind the consumed PR2312
inputs. The canonical JSON target hashes cover every composed output field.
The literal base tag names PR2312 width exchange plus coherent joint616;
SOURCE_COMMIT and SOURCE_MANIFEST identify the consumed source.
This generation receipt does not establish native phases, owner admission,
or a new exponent; those require their separate independently replayed
native and global receipts.
